clue.text: Hunt, wearing nursing uniform, is a prickly individual

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so this piece holds the next one inside it

parts.note: to hunt is to search
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
wearing a garment is being in it

explanation.surface: A huntsman in a nurse's uniform turns out to be a prickly character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' means being in a garment, giving IN; 'nursing' holds U, the NATO alphabet word uniform, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiny marine creature is literally a prickly living thing, hence a prickly individual.

clue.text: Dodgy OAPs look after gold in financial centre

indicators.note: look is placed after gold, so it comes second in this pair
something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so these letters are not to be trusted in their printed order

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
LO is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Crooked pensioners keep an eye on their gold in a banking hub.
explanation.walkthrough: OAPs are old-age pensioners in Britain; 'Dodgy' shuffles those letters, and 'after' sets look behind gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian city is the country's main business and stock-exchange hub.

clue.text: Soprano thrown out of bar in hail

indicators.note: being thrown out of somewhere means being removed, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: bar and save both mean except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: A singer is ejected from a pub during a hailstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means 'except', i.e. SAVE; 'thrown out of' removes its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is a Latin greeting, so it serves as a salutation like 'hail!'

clue.text: Again, bust chair?

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
bust is slang for arrest

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a broken chair has been broken once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical definition: split the answer as REAR REST, a seat for one's behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is jokingly a support for the bottom, a rest for the rear.

clue.text: Upset, start to reside in temporary building

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so the letter sits inside the building

parts.note: a hut is a simple temporary building

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at having to start living in a temporary building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes R from 'reside'; 'in' puts it inside HUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt and upset are synonyms describing someone whose feelings are wounded.

clue.text: Unusual tip to stop theft showing over-attention to detail

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: nicking is British slang for stealing

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An odd piece of advice for preventing burglary shows fussiness about details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' gives TPI; 'to stop' plugs it into the British slang word for theft, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitpicking is pedantic fault-finding over trivial points, i.e. excessive fussiness about minutiae.

clue.text: Georgia: country providing fossil fuel

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
country can mean land or soil, as in 'farming country'

explanation.surface: Georgia is a nation that supplies petroleum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgia' looks like the nation, but it is the US state abbreviation; 'country' is land.
explanation.definitionFit: This diesel-type oil is distilled from petroleum, a fuel formed from ancient organic remains.

clue.text: Nude Bristolian covers junk

indicators.note: the words cover, i.e. contain, the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A naked man from Bristol hides himself under rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' points to the letters running across nuDE BRIStolian.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or waste, the same as junk.

clue.text: Trump cut short meeting with prostitute, we hear, which is novel

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its end, here the last letter

parts.note: Ivana Trump was Donald Trump's first wife

indicators.note: says the word is judged by sound, so the slang term is entered as a garden tool

parts.note: ho is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A former president curtails a liaison with a sex worker, which is unprecedented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' is Ivana, not Donald; 'cut short' gives IVAN. 'we hear' turns HO into HOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott's Ivanhoe is a famous historical novel.

clue.text: Welcome females in the morning at European's great collection

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a word of welcome
F is female, doubled for the plural
AM means in the morning
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A greeting to the ladies one morning at a European's grand collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of fame is a gathering of celebrated people or exhibits honouring the greatest.

clue.text: Outside broadcast follows Frank

indicators.note: the broadcast word comes after the frank one, so it is second

parts.note: frank and open both mean candid
to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A TV outside broadcast follows a man named Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside broadcast' reads as one TV term, but 'Outside' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air events take place outdoors, not under a roof.

clue.text: Patrol old mills for a lot of money

indicators.note: milling grinds things up, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Police patrol old factory mills looking for a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mills' looks like a noun but is the verb signalling a rearrangement of PATROL + OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Top dollar is an idiom for the highest price, so a large sum.

clue.text: Ordnance is harmless in main transport channel

indicators.note: harmless means without ill, so the word ill is removed

parts.note: ordnance is military guns, i.e. artillery

explanation.surface: Military weaponry is safe when kept in a primary supply route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is harmless' means 'without ILL', taking ILL out of ARTILLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a major road or rail route, and also a main blood vessel.

clue.text: Pulls Emily Ratajkowski, for starters, in emotional movie

parts.note: tear and jerk both mean pull, two pulls together

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of each name

explanation.surface: A model pulls in fans in a sentimental film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulls' supplies two verbs, TEAR and JERK; 'for starters' gives ER, the initials of the model Emily Ratajkowski.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearjerker is a sentimental film designed to make the audience weep.

clue.text: Flowers might flower around spring and summer, primarily

parts.note: may and might both express possibility

indicators.note: the flower word goes around the two letters

parts.note: a bloom is a flower
S is the abbreviation for spring

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, taking the first letter

explanation.surface: Plants may come into bloom during spring and summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts S + S inside BLOOM; 'primarily' takes S from summer.
explanation.definitionFit: May blossom is the white hawthorn flowering in late spring.

clue.text: Developed thick skin about love, or just cold-hearted?

indicators.note: one piece wraps about the other, holding it inside

parts.note: callus as a verb means to form hardened skin
love is zero in tennis, i.e. O

explanation.surface: Someone toughened up emotionally over love, or is just heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside CALLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous describes an insensitive, unfeeling person, just as cold-hearted does.

clue.text: Usurer left Noah's, upset by his mode of transportation

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: Noah travelled in his ark

explanation.surface: A moneylender abandoned Noah's place, unsettled by his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges NOAHS to OANSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark lends money at extortionate interest, which is what a usurer does.

clue.text: A young explorer is getting expelled shortly, but is appealing

parts.note: Dora the Explorer is a children's cartoon girl

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, dropping the last letter

parts.note: blew means expelled, as breath or air

explanation.surface: A young adventurer faces expulsion soon, yet stays charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' removes the last letter of BLEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means charming or delightful, i.e. very attractive.

clue.text: Small, small person excited to cheat

parts.note: titch is British slang for a little person
up can mean excited or worked up

explanation.surface: A tiny person gets worked up enough to cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is everyday British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch-up is British slang for framing or swindling someone.

clue.text: Instruction to make payment to prevent heartless child collection

parts.note: to ban is to prevent

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a kid is a child
a raft is a large collection, as in 'a raft of ideas'

explanation.surface: An order to pay that stops a cruel child from collecting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the I out of KID.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank draft is a cheque guaranteed by a bank, an order to pay a sum.

clue.text: White privilege ultimately seen in small child having everything

indicators.note: something seen in another is inside it

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, used of a small child

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is used

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: White privilege shows up in a spoilt child who has it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White privilege' reads as a social phrase, but 'White' is the definition. 'seen in' puts E inside CUB.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker and pool, the white is the ball the player strikes with the cue.

clue.text: Wake up in bed containing Eccles and Oscar

indicators.note: the bed holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Eccles is the setter, who refers to themself as me
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The setter wakes in a bed alongside Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for ME; 'containing' puts it inside COT.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, i.e. to wake.

clue.text: Sunbathe naked to entertain Olympian

indicators.note: the words entertain, i.e. hold within them, the answer

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathes in the nude to amuse a Greek deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to entertain' points to letters running across sunbATHE NAked.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is one of the gods who live on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Pulls off tense clergyman

parts.note: to prise off something is to pry it, spelt pries
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone nervously removes a churchman's garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective but is the grammar abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister, a clergyman.

clue.text: Cooked steak with ham and eggs, at first, in hurry

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so these letters are mixed
at first takes the first letter

explanation.surface: Fried-up steak, ham and eggs gobbled down in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges STEAK + HAM to MAKEHAST; 'at first' adds the E of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To make haste is an idiom meaning to hurry.

clue.text: Overthrown monarchy welcomes son; he had lost his birthright

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the son goes inside
overthrown means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the UAE is a federation of hereditary monarchies

explanation.surface: A deposed royal house takes in a son who lost his inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overthrown' turns UAE (the United Arab Emirates) to EAU; 'welcomes' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau sold his birthright to his brother Jacob.

clue.text: South American bishop going to spa for day of relaxation

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Bath is an English spa town

explanation.surface: A South American cleric heads to a spa to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath, a city in south-west England, is famous for its Roman spa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest observed in Judaism and Christianity.

clue.text: Perhaps Charles is cycling in Scottish town

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end to the other

parts.note: Ray Charles was the singer; Ray is one example of a Charles

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man named Charles is out on his bike in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles' is a surname here: Ray Charles. 'is cycling' moves R from the front of RAY to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Friend of Dorothy drinking Burgundy perhaps in provincial capital

indicators.note: drinking takes the other piece inside

parts.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz
Ron Burgundy is the newsreader in the film Anchorman

explanation.surface: A gay man drinks wine, perhaps, in a Canadian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend of Dorothy' is slang for a gay man and 'Burgundy' suggests wine, but they are Toto and Ron Burgundy.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the capital of the Canadian province of Ontario.

clue.text: Route maps confused pest controller

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Muddled directions baffle the exterminator.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousetrap catches rodents, so it controls vermin.
